description: At night the Roman Theatre of Mérida rises floodlit out of the dark — the two-tiered scaenae frons with its marble columns glowing warm above the semicircular cavea, empty now of the festival crowds. Built in 16–15 BC under Agrippa for the capital of Lusitania, and seating 6,000, it has hosted the International Festival of Classical Theatre every summer since 1933. Under the stars the old stone carries its 2,000 years of acoustics alone.

prompts.prompt-r1.txt: Photorealistic artistic interpretation of the Roman Theatre of Mérida, Spain, at night. The ancient scaenae frons with its two tiers of marble columns rises floodlit warm against the dark night sky; the semicircular cavea seating tiers arc around the orchestra in shadow below. Empty stage, no performance in progress, no modern scaffolding. No identifiable people prominent. Subject centred so it survives a 4:5 centre crop. No text or brand logos anywhere, no on-image text at all.
